232	    exit 4
233	  fi
234	  rm -f "$a.run"
235	  if [ "$keep" = 1 ]; then
236	    sid=$(sed -n 1p "$a.session" 2>/dev/null)
237	    if [ -n "$sid" ]; then
238	      resume=$sid
239	      ctxb=$(jq -r '.ctx // empty' "$a.exit.json" 2>/dev/null)
240	    elif sid=$(hl_last_session "$role") && [ "$sid" = closed ]; then
241	      echo "harness: note: $role was closed after its last successful run; no session to resume — running fresh"
242	    elif [ -n "$sid" ]; then
243	      # the previous run died before it reported a session: fall back to the last successful one
244	      resume=$sid
245	      echo "harness: note: the previous run recorded no session; resuming the last successful one from progress.jsonl (${sid:0:8})"
246	    else
247	      echo "harness: note: no previous session for $role — running fresh"
248	    fi
249	  fi
250	  # a session file left by an earlier run must never be mistaken for this run's
251	  rm -f "$a.session"
252	  rm -f "$report"
253	  id="$(date +%s)-$$-$RANDOM"; start=$(date +%s)
254	  printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$start" > "$a.current"
255	  rm -f "$a.exit.json" "$a.pid"
256	  if [ "$role" = implementer ]; then verify_tool baseline implementer 2>/dev/null || rm -f .harness/verify/implementer.json; fi
257	  max_s=$(hl_max_s "$role")
258	  printf '%s\n' "$text" > "$a.prompt"
259	  hl_launch "$role" "$id" "$resume" "$max_s" "$ctxb" "$start_s" "$poll"
260	  deadline=$((start + (timeout + 999) / 1000))
261	  # no --timeout: wait for the run to end (its cap plus a margin for the watchdog kill and exit.json), so a
262	  # background `harness ask` returns exactly when the run does and the conductor's task notification fires
263	  [ "${ASK_TIMEOUT_SET:-0}" = 1 ] || deadline=$((start + max_s + 30))
264	  prev=$(date +%s); dl0=$deadline
265	  retried=0
266	  while :; do
267	    if hl_done "$role" "$id"; then
268	      if [ "$retried" = 0 ] && hl_resume_missing "$role"; then
269	        # the session is gone: one fresh run in the same ask; the dead sid must not stay the resume target
270	        retried=1
271	        echo "harness: resume of ${resume:0:8} failed, running fresh" >&2
272	        resume=""; ctxb=""
273	        hl_launch "$role" "$id" "" "$max_s" "" "$start_s" "$poll"
274	        continue
275	      fi
276	      hl_collect "$role"
277	    fi
278	    if ! hl_alive "$role"; then
279	      # the runner may still be writing exit.json (jq, mv) as its pid disappears: give it ~3 s
280	      g=0; while [ "$g" -lt 30 ] && ! hl_done "$role" "$id"; do sleep 0.1; g=$((g + 1)); done
281	      if hl_done "$role" "$id"; then continue; fi
282	      sid=$(sed -n 1p "$a.session" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-8)
283	      if [ -n "$sid" ]; then
284	        echo "harness: $role's run is gone without a result (killed?); --keep resumes session $sid"
285	      else
286	        echo "harness: $role's run is gone without a result (killed?); it recorded no session (--keep resumes the last successful one, if any)"
287	      fi
288	      exit 3
289	    fi
290	    now=$(date +%s)
291	    deadline=$(hl_deadline_bump "$prev" "$now" "$poll" "$deadline" "$max_s" "$dl0"); prev=$now
292	    if [ "$now" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
293	      if [ "$role" = implementer ] && [ -f "$report.pending" ]; then
294	        # the Stop hook has hidden the report while it verifies; the run is never killed at the deadline
295	        echo "harness: $role is still verifying (Stop hook running, $(cat .harness/verify/implementer.attempts 2>/dev/null || echo 0) failed attempt(s) so far, $((now - start))s); collect: harness report $role; stop: harness close $role --force" >&2
296	        exit 4
297	      fi
298	      echo "harness: $role is still running (pid $(hl_pid "$role"), $((now - start))s); collect: harness report $role; stop: harness close $role --force" >&2
299	      exit 4
300	    fi
301	    sleep "$poll"
302	  done
303	}
304	
305	# report_headless <role> — `harness report` for a headless role; always exits
306	report_headless() {
307	  local role=$1 report="$REPORT_DIR/$1.md"
308	  if hl_alive "$role"; then
309	    echo "harness: still running ($(( $(date +%s) - $(awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))s); harness wait $role blocks until done" >&2
310	    exit 4
311	  fi
312	  if [ ! -f "$ASK_DIR/$role.exit.json" ]; then
313	    echo "harness: no finished run for $role" >&2
314	    exit 3
315	  fi
316	  hl_collect "$role"
317	}
318	
319	# hl_kill <role> — stop the role's run: TERM the runner (it kills its tree and writes
320	# exit.json killed:signal), wait up to 5 s, then kill the tree
321	hl_kill() {
322	  local role=$1 pid i=0 id
323	  pid=$(hl_pid "$role"); id=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.pid" 2>/dev/null)
324	  digits_only "$pid" || return 0
325	  kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null
326	  while [ "$i" -lt 50 ]; do
327	    hl_alive "$role" || return 0
328	    sleep 0.1; i=$((i + 1))
329	  done
330	  kill_tree "$pid"; kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null
331	  return 0
332	}
333	
334	# hl_finish_close <role> <reason> — drop the conversation (--keep must not resume a session across
335	# a close), log
336	hl_finish_close() {
337	  local a="$ASK_DIR/$1"
338	  # .current ends the run slot: status shows "-" again (exit.json stays for the post-mortem)
339	  rm -f "$a.session" "$a.current"
340	  log_close "$1" "$2" headless
341	  echo "closed $1"
342	}
343	
344	# close_headless <role> <force> — close the role's run slot: kill a live run (--force)
345	close_headless() {
346	  local role=$1 force=$2 reason=manual
347	  if ! hl_alive "$role" && [ ! -f "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" ]; then
348	    die "$role is not running"
349	  fi
350	  if hl_alive "$role"; then
351	    if [ "$force" != 1 ]; then
352	      echo "harness: $role has a run in progress (pid $(hl_pid "$role")); not closing (use --force to kill it)" >&2
353	      return 4
354	    fi
355	    hl_kill "$role"
356	    reason=force_kill
357	  fi
358	  hl_finish_close "$role" "$reason"
359	}
360	
361	# hl_target <cmd> <target> — validate the role for wait/watch: sets ASK_AGENT; dies for an unknown one
362	hl_target() {
363	  case " $AGENTS " in
364	    *" $2 "*) ASK_AGENT=$2 ;;
365	    *) die "$1: unknown agent '$2' (expected one of: $AGENTS)" ;;
366	  esac
367	}
368	# hl_starting <role> <id> — the run was just launched and has not written its pid file yet
369	hl_starting() {
370	  local a="$ASK_DIR/$1" st
371	  grep -q "^$2 " "$a.pid" 2>/dev/null && return 1
372	  st=$(awk -v i="$2" 'NR == 1 && $1 == i { print $2 }' "$a.current" 2>/dev/null)
373	  digits_only "${st:-}" && [ $(( $(date +%s) - st )) -lt "${HARNESS_HL_START_S:-15}" ]
374	}
375	
376	# cmd_wait <role> [--timeout ms] — block until the target's run ends; never collects.
377	# 0 done (exit.json carries the ask), 3 no ask / run gone without a result, 4 timeout.
378	cmd_wait() {
379	  local t=${1:-} timeout="" role id a start deadline dl0 max_s prev now g poll=${HARNESS_POLL_SEC:-2}
380	  [ -n "$t" ] || usage
381	  shift
382	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
383	    case "$1" in
384	      --timeout) case "${2:-}" in ''|*[!0-9]*|0) die "--timeout needs a number of milliseconds" ;; esac; timeout=$2; shift 2 ;;
385	      *) usage ;;
386	    esac
387	  done
388	  hl_target wait "$t"
389	  role=$ASK_AGENT; a="$ASK_DIR/$role"
390	  id=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$a.current" 2>/dev/null)
391	  [ -n "$id" ] || { echo "harness: no ask for $role" >&2; exit 3; }
392	  [ -n "$timeout" ] || timeout=$(( $(hl_max_s "$role") * 1000 ))
393	  start=$(date +%s); deadline=$((start + (timeout + 999) / 1000)); prev=$start; dl0=$deadline; max_s=$(hl_max_s "$role")
394	  while :; do
395	    if hl_done "$role" "$id"; then echo "done; collect: harness report $role"; exit 0; fi
396	    if ! hl_alive "$role" && ! hl_starting "$role" "$id"; then
397	      # the runner may still be writing exit.json as its pid disappears: the same ~3 s grace as ask
398	      g=0; while [ "$g" -lt 30 ] && ! hl_done "$role" "$id"; do sleep 0.1; g=$((g + 1)); done
399	      if hl_done "$role" "$id"; then continue; fi
400	      echo "harness: $role's run is gone without a result (killed?); harness report $role explains" >&2
401	      exit 3
402	    fi
403	    now=$(date +%s)
404	    deadline=$(hl_deadline_bump "$prev" "$now" "$poll" "$deadline" "$max_s" "$dl0"); prev=$now
405	    if [ "$now" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
406	      echo "harness: $role is still running ($((now - start))s waited); harness wait $role again, or harness close $role --force" >&2
407	      exit 4
408	    fi
409	    sleep "$poll"
410	  done
411	}
412	
413	# hl_stream_of <role> — the raw stream of the role's current/last run (empty when unknown): .stream when its
414	# id is the current ask, else exit.json's stream_log; a rotated stream is <raw>.gz
415	hl_stream_of() {
416	  local a="$ASK_DIR/$1" raw cur
417	  cur=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$a.current" 2>/dev/null)
418	  raw=$(awk -v i="$cur" 'NR == 1 && $1 == i { print $2 }' "$a.stream" 2>/dev/null)
419	  [ -n "$raw" ] || raw=$(jq -r '.stream_log // empty' "$a.exit.json" 2>/dev/null)
420	  [ -n "$raw" ] || raw=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' "$a.stream" 2>/dev/null)
421	  printf '%s' "$raw"
422	}
423	
424	hl_stream_id() { awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$ASK_DIR/$1.stream" 2>/dev/null; }
425	
426	# cmd_watch <role> [-n N] — human only: a live run as a redrawn dashboard (lib/harness-dash.sh), or print the last N
427	# (default 40) rendered lines of a finished one. 0 ok, 1 refused (not a tty), 3 no stream known.
428	cmd_watch() {
429	  local t=${1:-} n=40 nset="" role raw i id
430	  [ -n "$t" ] || usage
431	  shift
432	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
433	    case "$1" in
434	      -n) case "${2:-}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) die "-n needs a number of lines" ;; esac; n=$2; nset=1; shift 2 ;;
435	      *) usage ;;
436	    esac
437	  done
438	  [ -t 1 ] || die "watch is for a human terminal; the conductor reads the report"
439	  hl_target watch "$t"
440	  role=$ASK_AGENT
441	  id=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" 2>/dev/null)
442	  raw=$(hl_stream_of "$role"); i=0
443	  # a run that is still starting has not announced its stream yet: give it a few seconds
444	  while [ "$(hl_stream_id "$role")" != "$id" ] && [ "$i" -lt 100 ] && { hl_alive "$role" || hl_starting "$role" "$id"; }; do
445	    sleep 0.2; i=$((i + 1)); raw=$(hl_stream_of "$role")
446	  done
447	  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then echo "harness: no stream known for $t" >&2; exit 3; fi
448	  # -n N (or a rotated .gz stream): one-shot plain tail of a finished run (scrollback text; reflows by itself)
449	  if { [ -n "$nset" ] || [ ! -f "$raw" ]; } && ! hl_alive "$role"; then
450	    if [ -f "$raw" ]; then harness-view < "$raw" | tail -n "$n"
451	    elif [ -f "$raw.gz" ]; then gzip -dc "$raw.gz" | harness-view | tail -n "$n"
452	    else echo "harness: stream $raw is gone" >&2; exit 3; fi
453	    exit 0
454	  fi
455	  dash_watch "$role" "$raw" "$id"
456	  exit 0
457	}

# harness-headless.sh — the headless runner glue (decisions 0007, 0011): hl_*, ask/report/close_headless.
# Sourced eagerly by bin/harness (see the loader there): definitions only, no side effects.
# Shared helpers (die, ...) stay in bin/harness and resolve at call time.

# --- headless runner (decision 0007) --------------------------------------------------------------
# `harness ask` writes the instruction to a file and starts `harness-run` (claude -p, stream-json)
# detached in the background. Completion = the run's .harness/asks/<role>.exit.json carrying this
# ask-id. A human watches a run with `harness watch <role>` in any terminal.

# env a background run must not inherit: the conductor's Claude identity (a denylist, not
# env -i: API keys, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, proxies, PATH, HOME and TMPDIR pass through)
HL_ENV_STRIP="-u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT -u CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -u CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION"
HL_ENV_STRIP="$HL_ENV_STRIP -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED -u CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET -u CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN -u CLAUDE_PID -u CLAUDE_EFFORT -u CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH"

# hl_alive <role> — a harness-run for the role is running (pid file, live harness-run process)
hl_alive() {
  local f="$ASK_DIR/$1.pid" id pid
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 1
  read -r id pid _ < "$f"
  digits_only "${pid:-}" && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  ps -p "$pid" -o command= 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'harness-run'
}
# hl_last_session <role> — session id of the role's latest *successful* headless run (progress
# line with result "success" and a session). Old rows with an ask_id (the removed --worktree asks)
# are ignored, as in last_ask_record. A close event of the role is a boundary: when one came after the last such run, print "closed" instead (no session id looks like that).
hl_last_session() {
  [ -f "$JSONL" ] || return 1
  tail -n 200 "$JSONL" 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -R -n -r --arg r "$1" '
        reduce (inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object")) as $e ({sid: "", closed: false};
          if $e.event == "close" then (if $e.role == $r and ($e.ask_id // "") == "" then {sid: "", closed: true} else . end)
          elif ($e.ask_id // "") != "" then .
          elif $e.agent == $r and $e.runner == "headless" and $e.result == "success" and (($e.session // "") != "") then {sid: $e.session, closed: false}
          else . end)
        | if .sid != "" then .sid elif .closed then "closed" else empty end' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep .
}
hl_pid() { awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' "$ASK_DIR/$1.pid" 2>/dev/null; }
# hl_done <role> <ask-id> — exit.json exists for that ask
hl_done() { grep -q "\"ask_id\":\"$2\"" "$ASK_DIR/$1.exit.json" 2>/dev/null; }

# hl_progress_obj <role> <t0> — extra progress.jsonl fields of the role's last run, as one
# JSON object (keys session / ctx_after are consumed by the caller)
hl_progress_obj() {
  local role=$1 t0=${2:-} ej="$ASK_DIR/$1.exit.json" id resume=false
  id=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -z "$(sed -n 's/^resume=//p' "$ASK_DIR/$role.run" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)" ] || resume=true
  if [ -f "$ej" ] && { [ -z "$id" ] || hl_done "$role" "$id"; }; then
    jq -c --argjson resume "$resume" --argjson t0 "$(num_or_null "$t0")" '
      {runner: "headless", cost_usd: (.cost_usd // null), turns: (.num_turns // null), result: (.result // null),
       denials: (.denials // null), stream_log: (.stream_log // null), resume: $resume,
       startup_s: (if (.t_init | type) == "number" and $t0 != null then (.t_init - $t0) else null end),
       session: (.session_id // ""), ctx_after: (.ctx // "")}' "$ej" 2>/dev/null && return 0
  fi
  jq -n -c --argjson resume "$resume" '{runner: "headless", resume: $resume, session: "", ctx_after: ""}'
}

# hl_status_line <role> status|progress — one line for `harness status` / progress.md. Keyed on the
# run state
hl_status_line() {
  local role=$1 mode=$2 st el ctx
  if hl_alive "$role"; then st=running
  elif [ -f "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" ]; then st=idle
  else
    if [ "$mode" = status ]; then printf '%-12s %s\n' "$role" "-"; else printf '%s -' "$role"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  ctx=$(jq -r '.ctx // empty' "$ASK_DIR/$role.exit.json" 2>/dev/null)
  el=""
  [ "$st" != running ] || el=$(( $(date +%s) - $(awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))
  if [ "$mode" = status ]; then
    if [ "$st" = running ]; then printf '%-12s %-8s hl %ss\n' "$role" "$st" "$el"
    else printf '%-12s %-8s hl ctx %s\n' "$role" "$st" "$(fmt_ctx "$ctx")"; fi
  else
    printf '%s %s ctx %s hl' "$role" "$st" "$(fmt_ctx "$ctx")"
  fi
}

# hl_collect <role> — a finished run (exit.json present): print the report or explain, exit.
# First match wins (spec §3). Never returns.
hl_collect() {
  local role=$1 ej="$ASK_DIR/$1.exit.json" report="$REPORT_DIR/$1.md" cur="$ASK_DIR/$1.current"
  local rc res iserr killed sid tinit perm ejc denied
  ejc=$(cat "$ej" 2>/dev/null)   # one read
  rc=$(jq -r '.rc // empty' <<<"$ejc" 2>/dev/null); res=$(jq -r '.result // empty' <<<"$ejc" 2>/dev/null)
  iserr=$(jq -r '.is_error // false' <<<"$ejc" 2>/dev/null); killed=$(jq -r '.killed // empty' <<<"$ejc" 2>/dev/null)
  sid=$(jq -r '(.session_id // "") | .[0:8]' <<<"$ejc" 2>/dev/null); tinit=$(jq -r '.t_init // empty' <<<"$ejc" 2>/dev/null)
  perm=$(jq -r '.perm // empty' <<<"$ejc" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -n "$perm" ] && [ "$perm" != auto ]; then
    echo "harness: warning: $role ran with permission mode '$perm', not auto; tools may have been denied (see harness watch)" >&2
  fi
  denied=$(jq -r '(.denied // [])[] | "  - \(.tool): \(.input)\(if (.reason // "") != "" then " (" + .reason + ")" else "" end)"' <<<"$ejc" 2>/dev/null)
  restore_interrupted "$role" "$report"
  if [ -f "$report" ] && { [ ! -f "$cur" ] || [ ! "$report" -ot "$cur" ]; }; then
    [ -z "$denied" ] || printf 'harness: note: %s denied tool call(s):\n%s\n' "$(grep -c . <<<"$denied")" "$denied" >&2
    if { [ -n "$rc" ] && [ "$rc" != 0 ]; } || [ "$iserr" = true ]; then
      echo "harness: note: $role's run ended with ${res:-no result} (rc ${rc:-?}) but wrote a report" >&2
    fi
    finish_report "$role" "$report"
  fi
  if [ "$res" = error_max_turns ]; then
    echo "harness: $role stopped at the max-turns limit without a report; continue with: harness ask $role '...' --keep"
    hl_view_tail "$role" 30; exit 3
  fi
  if [ -n "$killed" ]; then
    echo "harness: $role's run was killed ($killed); --keep resumes session ${sid:-?}"
    exit 3
  fi
  if [ "$rc" = 127 ] || [ -z "$tinit" ]; then
    echo "harness: $role's claude did not start (rc ${rc:-?}):" >&2
    tail -n 20 "$ASK_DIR/$role.err" 2>/dev/null >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$iserr" = true ] || [ -n "$res" -a "$res" != success ] || { [ -n "$rc" ] && [ "$rc" != 0 ]; }; then
    echo "harness: $role's worker ended with ${res:-error} (rc ${rc:-?}) and wrote no report"
    tail -n 20 "$ASK_DIR/$role.err" 2>/dev/null
    hl_view_tail "$role" 30; exit 3
  fi
  # permissions blocked the worker and it wrote nothing: there is no answer to relay (exit 2), only when the run ended without errors
  if [ -n "$denied" ] && [ -z "$killed" ] && [ -n "$tinit" ]; then
    printf 'harness: %s was denied %s tool call(s) and wrote no report; nothing to answer. Re-ask with a changed brief:\n%s\n' \
      "$role" "$(grep -c . <<<"$denied")" "$denied"
    hl_view_tail "$role" 30; exit 2
  fi
  echo "harness: $role finished without a report at $report; collect: harness report $role"
  hl_view_tail "$role" 30; exit 3
}
# hl_view_tail <role> <n> — the last n lines the run showed: the rendered stream
hl_view_tail() {
  local role=$1 n=${2:-30} raw
  raw=$(jq -r '.stream_log // empty' "$ASK_DIR/$role.exit.json" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$raw" ] || raw=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.stream" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -n "$raw" ] && [ -f "$raw" ]; then harness-view < "$raw" 2>/dev/null | tail -n "$n"; fi
  return 0
}

# hl_spawn_bg <role> <id> <root> — start harness-run detached from this process tree: a double fork
# (the subshell exits at once, so the run is reparented to init and ask_finish's kill_tree never
# reaches it) in a new session (no controlling tty, and a pgid kill of the caller's call misses it).
# There is no setsid binary on macOS: perl does it. HARNESS_HL_NO_PERL=1 forces the fallback (tests).
# Under this spawn harness-run's INT/HUP traps are inert (an async start ignores INT, nohup ignores
# HUP); only TERM reaches it, which is what hl_kill sends. Intended.
hl_spawn_bg() {
  local role=$1 id=$2 root=$3 log
  case "$ASK_DIR" in /*) log=$ASK_DIR ;; *) log=$root/$ASK_DIR ;; esac
  log=$log/$role.runner.log
  if [ "${HARNESS_HL_NO_PERL:-}" != 1 ] && command -v perl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ( cd "$root" && exec env $HL_ENV_STRIP HARNESS_ROLE=worker CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=160000 \
        nohup perl -MPOSIX -e 'POSIX::setsid() or die "setsid: $!"; exec @ARGV or die "exec: $!"' \
        harness-run "$role" "$id" "$root" </dev/null >>"$log" 2>&1 & )
  else
    # no perl: its own process group through job control (the session stays shared)
    ( cd "$root" || exit 1; set -m
      env $HL_ENV_STRIP HARNESS_ROLE=worker CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=160000 \
        nohup harness-run "$role" "$id" "$root" </dev/null >>"$log" 2>&1 & )
  fi
}

# hl_launch <role> <id> <resume> <max_s> <ctxb> <start_s> <poll> — write the run file, start
# harness-run detached in the background and wait for its pid file; exits 1 when it never starts.
hl_launch() {
  local role=$1 id=$2 resume=$3 max_s=$4 ctxb=$5 start_s=$6 poll=$7 a="$ASK_DIR/$1" s0 root
  root=$(pwd -P)
  rm -f "$a.exit.json" "$a.pid"
  printf 'resume=%s\nmax_s=%s\nctx_before=%s\n' "$resume" "$max_s" "$ctxb" > "$a.run"
  hl_spawn_bg "$role" "$id" "$root"
  # the run announces itself with its pid file
  s0=$(date +%s)
  until grep -q "^$id " "$a.pid" 2>/dev/null || hl_done "$role" "$id"; do
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - s0 )) -ge "$start_s" ]; then
      echo "harness: $role's background run did not start in $start_s s; runner log:" >&2
      tail -n 20 "$a.runner.log" >&2 2>/dev/null
      exit 1
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
}
# hl_resume_missing <role> — the finished run was a --resume that produced no init event because
# claude could not find the conversation (real claude: result-only stream, error_during_execution)
hl_resume_missing() {
  local role=$1 a="$ASK_DIR/$1" raw
  [ -n "$(sed -n 's/^resume=//p' "$a.run" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)" ] || return 1
  [ -z "$(jq -r '.t_init // empty' "$a.exit.json" 2>/dev/null)" ] || return 1
  raw=$(jq -r '.stream_log // empty' "$a.exit.json" 2>/dev/null)
  grep -qi 'no conversation found' "$a.err" 2>/dev/null && return 0
  [ -z "$raw" ] || grep -qi 'no conversation found' "$raw" 2>/dev/null
}

# hl_max_s <role> — the role's headless run cap in seconds: env, then config headless_max_minutes, then the default
hl_max_s() {
  local m=${HARNESS_HL_MAX_S:-}
  digits_only "$m" && { echo "$m"; return 0; }
  m=$(jq -r '.headless_max_minutes // empty' "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
  digits_only "$m" && { echo $((m * 60)); return 0; }
  if [ "$1" = implementer ]; then echo "$HARNESS_HL_MAX_S_IMPLEMENTER_DEFAULT"; else echo "$HARNESS_HL_MAX_S_DEFAULT"; fi
}

# hl_clock_gap <prev-epoch> <now-epoch> <poll-s> — print the seconds to add to a deadline when the
# wall clock jumped between two polls (laptop sleep): a gap above 5x the poll interval + 5 s counts as a
# suspend; 0 otherwise. Pure arithmetic, so tests inject the timestamps.
hl_clock_gap() {
  awk -v p="$1" -v n="$2" -v i="${3:-2}" 'BEGIN { g = n - p; if (g > 5 * i + 5) printf "%d\n", g; else print 0 }'
}
# hl_deadline_bump <prev> <now> <poll> <deadline> [<cap-s> <deadline0>] — print the (possibly extended) deadline;
# one stderr line when it moved. With a cap, one bump is at most <cap-s> and all bumps together at most
# 2x<cap-s> over <deadline0> (the deadline before any bump), so a bogus clock jump cannot keep an ask alive forever.
hl_deadline_bump() {
  local g=0 cap=${5:-} d0=${6:-$4} room
  g=$(hl_clock_gap "$1" "$2" "$3")
  case "$cap" in ''|*[!0-9]*) cap=0 ;; esac
  if [ "$g" -gt 0 ] && [ "$cap" -gt 0 ]; then
    [ "$g" -le "$cap" ] || g=$cap
    room=$((2 * cap - ($4 - d0)))
    [ "$room" -gt 0 ] || room=0
    [ "$g" -le "$room" ] || g=$room
  fi
  if [ "$g" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "harness: clock jumped ${g}s (sleep?); deadline extended" >&2
    echo $(($4 + g))
  else
    echo "$4"
  fi
}

# ask_headless <role> <text> <timeout-ms> <keep> — the whole headless ask; always exits
ask_headless() {
  local role=$1 text=$2 timeout=$3 keep=$4 id start retried resume="" sid max_s ctxb="" report="$REPORT_DIR/$1.md"
  local a="$ASK_DIR/$role" now prev deadline dl0 poll=${HARNESS_POLL_SEC:-2} start_s=${HARNESS_HL_START_S:-15} s0 g
  mkdir -p "$ASK_DIR" "$REPORT_DIR" "$LOG_DIR"
  if hl_alive "$role"; then
    echo "harness: $role is still running (pid $(hl_pid "$role")); nothing sent. Collect with: harness report $role; stop: harness close $role --force" >&2
    exit 4
  fi
  rm -f "$a.run"
  if [ "$keep" = 1 ]; then
    sid=$(sed -n 1p "$a.session" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$sid" ]; then
      resume=$sid
      ctxb=$(jq -r '.ctx // empty' "$a.exit.json" 2>/dev/null)
    elif sid=$(hl_last_session "$role") && [ "$sid" = closed ]; then
      echo "harness: note: $role was closed after its last successful run; no session to resume — running fresh"
    elif [ -n "$sid" ]; then
      # the previous run died before it reported a session: fall back to the last successful one
      resume=$sid
      echo "harness: note: the previous run recorded no session; resuming the last successful one from progress.jsonl (${sid:0:8})"
    else
      echo "harness: note: no previous session for $role — running fresh"
    fi
  fi
  # a session file left by an earlier run must never be mistaken for this run's
  rm -f "$a.session"
  rm -f "$report"
  id="$(date +%s)-$$-$RANDOM"; start=$(date +%s)
  printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$start" > "$a.current"
  rm -f "$a.exit.json" "$a.pid"
  if [ "$role" = implementer ]; then verify_tool baseline implementer 2>/dev/null || rm -f .harness/verify/implementer.json; fi
  max_s=$(hl_max_s "$role")
  printf '%s\n' "$text" > "$a.prompt"
  hl_launch "$role" "$id" "$resume" "$max_s" "$ctxb" "$start_s" "$poll"
  deadline=$((start + (timeout + 999) / 1000))
  # no --timeout: wait for the run to end (its cap plus a margin for the watchdog kill and exit.json), so a
  # background `harness ask` returns exactly when the run does and the conductor's task notification fires
  [ "${ASK_TIMEOUT_SET:-0}" = 1 ] || deadline=$((start + max_s + 30))
  prev=$(date +%s); dl0=$deadline
  retried=0
  while :; do
    if hl_done "$role" "$id"; then
      if [ "$retried" = 0 ] && hl_resume_missing "$role"; then
        # the session is gone: one fresh run in the same ask; the dead sid must not stay the resume target
        retried=1
        echo "harness: resume of ${resume:0:8} failed, running fresh" >&2
        resume=""; ctxb=""
        hl_launch "$role" "$id" "" "$max_s" "" "$start_s" "$poll"
        continue
      fi
      hl_collect "$role"
    fi
    if ! hl_alive "$role"; then
      # the runner may still be writing exit.json (jq, mv) as its pid disappears: give it ~3 s
      g=0; while [ "$g" -lt 30 ] && ! hl_done "$role" "$id"; do sleep 0.1; g=$((g + 1)); done
      if hl_done "$role" "$id"; then continue; fi
      sid=$(sed -n 1p "$a.session" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-8)
      if [ -n "$sid" ]; then
        echo "harness: $role's run is gone without a result (killed?); --keep resumes session $sid"
      else
        echo "harness: $role's run is gone without a result (killed?); it recorded no session (--keep resumes the last successful one, if any)"
      fi
      exit 3
    fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    deadline=$(hl_deadline_bump "$prev" "$now" "$poll" "$deadline" "$max_s" "$dl0"); prev=$now
    if [ "$now" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
      if [ "$role" = implementer ] && [ -f "$report.pending" ]; then
        # the Stop hook has hidden the report while it verifies; the run is never killed at the deadline
        echo "harness: $role is still verifying (Stop hook running, $(cat .harness/verify/implementer.attempts 2>/dev/null || echo 0) failed attempt(s) so far, $((now - start))s); collect: harness report $role; stop: harness close $role --force" >&2
        exit 4
      fi
      echo "harness: $role is still running (pid $(hl_pid "$role"), $((now - start))s); collect: harness report $role; stop: harness close $role --force" >&2
      exit 4
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
}

# report_headless <role> — `harness report` for a headless role; always exits
report_headless() {
  local role=$1 report="$REPORT_DIR/$1.md"
  if hl_alive "$role"; then
    echo "harness: still running ($(( $(date +%s) - $(awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))s); harness wait $role blocks until done" >&2
    exit 4
  fi
  if [ ! -f "$ASK_DIR/$role.exit.json" ]; then
    echo "harness: no finished run for $role" >&2
    exit 3
  fi
  hl_collect "$role"
}

# hl_kill <role> — stop the role's run: TERM the runner (it kills its tree and writes
# exit.json killed:signal), wait up to 5 s, then kill the tree
hl_kill() {
  local role=$1 pid i=0 id
  pid=$(hl_pid "$role"); id=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.pid" 2>/dev/null)
  digits_only "$pid" || return 0
  kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null
  while [ "$i" -lt 50 ]; do
    hl_alive "$role" || return 0
    sleep 0.1; i=$((i + 1))
  done
  kill_tree "$pid"; kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}

# hl_finish_close <role> <reason> — drop the conversation (--keep must not resume a session across
# a close), log
hl_finish_close() {
  local a="$ASK_DIR/$1"
  # .current ends the run slot: status shows "-" again (exit.json stays for the post-mortem)
  rm -f "$a.session" "$a.current"
  log_close "$1" "$2" headless
  echo "closed $1"
}

# close_headless <role> <force> — close the role's run slot: kill a live run (--force)
close_headless() {
  local role=$1 force=$2 reason=manual
  if ! hl_alive "$role" && [ ! -f "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" ]; then
    die "$role is not running"
  fi
  if hl_alive "$role"; then
    if [ "$force" != 1 ]; then
      echo "harness: $role has a run in progress (pid $(hl_pid "$role")); not closing (use --force to kill it)" >&2
      return 4
    fi
    hl_kill "$role"
    reason=force_kill
  fi
  hl_finish_close "$role" "$reason"
}

# hl_target <cmd> <target> — validate the role for wait/watch: sets ASK_AGENT; dies for an unknown one
hl_target() {
  case " $AGENTS " in
    *" $2 "*) ASK_AGENT=$2 ;;
    *) die "$1: unknown agent '$2' (expected one of: $AGENTS)" ;;
  esac
}
# hl_starting <role> <id> — the run was just launched and has not written its pid file yet
hl_starting() {
  local a="$ASK_DIR/$1" st
  grep -q "^$2 " "$a.pid" 2>/dev/null && return 1
  st=$(awk -v i="$2" 'NR == 1 && $1 == i { print $2 }' "$a.current" 2>/dev/null)
  digits_only "${st:-}" && [ $(( $(date +%s) - st )) -lt "${HARNESS_HL_START_S:-15}" ]
}

# cmd_wait <role> [--timeout ms] — block until the target's run ends; never collects.
# 0 done (exit.json carries the ask), 3 no ask / run gone without a result, 4 timeout.
cmd_wait() {
  local t=${1:-} timeout="" role id a start deadline dl0 max_s prev now g poll=${HARNESS_POLL_SEC:-2}
  [ -n "$t" ] || usage
  shift
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --timeout) case "${2:-}" in ''|*[!0-9]*|0) die "--timeout needs a number of milliseconds" ;; esac; timeout=$2; shift 2 ;;
      *) usage ;;
    esac
  done
  hl_target wait "$t"
  role=$ASK_AGENT; a="$ASK_DIR/$role"
  id=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$a.current" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$id" ] || { echo "harness: no ask for $role" >&2; exit 3; }
  [ -n "$timeout" ] || timeout=$(( $(hl_max_s "$role") * 1000 ))
  start=$(date +%s); deadline=$((start + (timeout + 999) / 1000)); prev=$start; dl0=$deadline; max_s=$(hl_max_s "$role")
  while :; do
    if hl_done "$role" "$id"; then echo "done; collect: harness report $role"; exit 0; fi
    if ! hl_alive "$role" && ! hl_starting "$role" "$id"; then
      # the runner may still be writing exit.json as its pid disappears: the same ~3 s grace as ask
      g=0; while [ "$g" -lt 30 ] && ! hl_done "$role" "$id"; do sleep 0.1; g=$((g + 1)); done
      if hl_done "$role" "$id"; then continue; fi
      echo "harness: $role's run is gone without a result (killed?); harness report $role explains" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    deadline=$(hl_deadline_bump "$prev" "$now" "$poll" "$deadline" "$max_s" "$dl0"); prev=$now
    if [ "$now" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
      echo "harness: $role is still running ($((now - start))s waited); harness wait $role again, or harness close $role --force" >&2
      exit 4
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
}

# hl_stream_of <role> — the raw stream of the role's current/last run (empty when unknown): .stream when its
# id is the current ask, else exit.json's stream_log; a rotated stream is <raw>.gz
hl_stream_of() {
  local a="$ASK_DIR/$1" raw cur
  cur=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$a.current" 2>/dev/null)
  raw=$(awk -v i="$cur" 'NR == 1 && $1 == i { print $2 }' "$a.stream" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$raw" ] || raw=$(jq -r '.stream_log // empty' "$a.exit.json" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$raw" ] || raw=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' "$a.stream" 2>/dev/null)
  printf '%s' "$raw"
}

hl_stream_id() { awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$ASK_DIR/$1.stream" 2>/dev/null; }

# cmd_watch <role> [-n N] — human only: a live run as a redrawn dashboard (lib/harness-dash.sh), or print the last N
# (default 40) rendered lines of a finished one. 0 ok, 1 refused (not a tty), 3 no stream known.
cmd_watch() {
  local t=${1:-} n=40 nset="" role raw i id
  [ -n "$t" ] || usage
  shift
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      -n) case "${2:-}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) die "-n needs a number of lines" ;; esac; n=$2; nset=1; shift 2 ;;
      *) usage ;;
    esac
  done
  [ -t 1 ] || die "watch is for a human terminal; the conductor reads the report"
  hl_target watch "$t"
  role=$ASK_AGENT
  id=$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$ASK_DIR/$role.current" 2>/dev/null)
  raw=$(hl_stream_of "$role"); i=0
  # a run that is still starting has not announced its stream yet: give it a few seconds
  while [ "$(hl_stream_id "$role")" != "$id" ] && [ "$i" -lt 100 ] && { hl_alive "$role" || hl_starting "$role" "$id"; }; do
    sleep 0.2; i=$((i + 1)); raw=$(hl_stream_of "$role")
  done
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then echo "harness: no stream known for $t" >&2; exit 3; fi
  # -n N (or a rotated .gz stream): one-shot plain tail of a finished run (scrollback text; reflows by itself)
  if { [ -n "$nset" ] || [ ! -f "$raw" ]; } && ! hl_alive "$role"; then
    if [ -f "$raw" ]; then harness-view < "$raw" | tail -n "$n"
    elif [ -f "$raw.gz" ]; then gzip -dc "$raw.gz" | harness-view | tail -n "$n"
    else echo "harness: stream $raw is gone" >&2; exit 3; fi
    exit 0
  fi
  dash_watch "$role" "$raw" "$id"
  exit 0
}

1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# Structure of the bin/harness + lib/*.sh split. Run: /bin/bash tests/harness-split.test.sh
     3	set -u
     4	HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
     5	ROOT=$HERE/..
     6	pass=0
     7	fail=0
     8	WORKS=""
     9	trap 'for d in $WORKS; do rm -rf "$d"; done' EXIT
    10	OUT=""
    11	check() { local label=$1; shift; if "$@"; then pass=$((pass + 1)); else fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL [$label]: $OUT"; fi; }
    12	
    13	# lib_named SCRIPT NAME — NAME is in SCRIPT's `for m in …` loader list
    14	lib_named() { [ -n "$2" ] && grep -E '^for m in ' "$1" | head -1 | grep -qw -- "$2"; }
    15	no_glob() { ! printf '%s' "$1" | grep -qE 'lib/\*|harness-\*'; }
    16	not() { ! "$@"; }
    17	# eager_ok SCRIPT — one `# end loader` marker, below the first function definition's line (so it cannot
    18	# sit at EOF or after a lazy function); >=1 harness-*.sh source line, all above the marker.
    19	# Limit: a textual check only; a source via a variable or eval is not detected.
    20	eager_ok() {
    21	  local mark srcs n fn
    22	  mark=$(grep -n '^# end loader$' "$1" | cut -d: -f1)
    23	  case $mark in ''|*[!0-9]*) OUT="$1: need exactly one '# end loader' marker"; return 1 ;; esac
    24	  fn=$(grep -nE '^([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\(\) *\{|function )' "$1" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    25	  if [ -n "$fn" ] && [ "$mark" -gt "$fn" ]; then OUT="$1: '# end loader' (line $mark) is below the first function (line $fn)"; return 1; fi
    26	  srcs=$(grep -nvE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$1" | grep -E '^[0-9]+:([^#]*[;&|[:space:]])?(\.|source)[[:space:]]+[^#]*harness-' | cut -d: -f1)
    27	  [ -n "$srcs" ] || { OUT="$1: no lib source found"; return 1; }
    28	  for n in $srcs; do
    29	    [ "$n" -lt "$mark" ] || { OUT="$1:$n sources a lib after '# end loader' (line $mark)"; return 1; }
    30	  done
    31	}
    32	# all_listed SCRIPT LIBDIR — every LIBDIR/harness-*.sh is in SCRIPT's loader list
    33	all_listed() {
    34	  local f b
    35	  for f in "$2"/harness-*.sh; do
    36	    b=$(basename "$f" .sh)
    37	    lib_named "$1" "${b#harness-}" || { OUT="${b#harness-} missing from loader list"; return 1; }
    38	  done
    39	}
    40	
    41	# top-level function names of a file (column-0 `name() {`)
    42	fnames() { grep -oE '^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*\(\)' "$1" | sed 's/()$//'; }
    43	
    44	LIBS=$(ls "$ROOT"/lib/harness-*.sh)
    45	for f in $LIBS; do
    46	  b=$(basename "$f" .sh); m=${b#harness-}
    47	  check "$b: bash -n" bash -n "$f"
    48	  # every function name is defined exactly once across bin/harness and lib/*.sh
    49	  OUT=$(for n in $(fnames "$f"); do
    50	          c=$(cat "$ROOT/bin/harness" $LIBS | grep -cE "^$n\(\)")
    51	          [ "$c" -eq 1 ] || echo "$n defined $c times"
    52	        done)
    53	  check "$b: each function defined once" [ -z "$OUT" ]
    54	  # sourcing defines only: no output, no exit, no side effects on the cwd
    55	  d=$(mktemp -d); WORKS="$WORKS $d"
    56	  OUT=$(cd "$d" && . "$f" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?")
    57	  check "$b: sourcing prints nothing and exits 0" [ "$OUT" = "rc=0" ]
    58	  OUT=$(ls -A "$d")
    59	  check "$b: sourcing creates no files" [ -z "$OUT" ]
    60	  # the loader names it explicitly (the loop list)
    61	  OUT=$(grep -n '^for m in ' "$ROOT/bin/harness" | head -1)
    62	  check "$b: named in the loader list" lib_named "$ROOT/bin/harness" "$m"
    63	done
    64	load=$(grep -n '^for m in ' "$ROOT/bin/harness" | head -1)
    65	loadn=${load%%:*}
    66	firstfn=$(grep -nE '^[a-z_]+\(\) *\{' "$ROOT/bin/harness" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    67	OUT="loader at $loadn, first function at $firstfn"
    68	check "loader precedes the first function in bin/harness" [ "$loadn" -lt "$firstfn" ]
    69	# no glob in the loader
    70	OUT=$(sed -n "${loadn},$((loadn+3))p" "$ROOT/bin/harness")
    71	check "loader lists files, not a glob" no_glob "$OUT"
    72	
    73	# eager loading, structurally: every source of a harness-*.sh sits above `# end loader`, nowhere else
    74	for s in bin/harness bin/harness-verify claude/hooks/conductor-gate.sh claude/hooks/conductor-resume.sh; do
    75	  OUT=""
    76	  check "$s: libs sourced only inside the loader block" eager_ok "$ROOT/$s"
    77	done
    78	check "bin/harness loads every lib/harness-*.sh" all_listed "$ROOT/bin/harness" "$ROOT/lib"
    79	# test the test: a dropped list entry and a lazy source must both be caught
    80	M=$(mktemp -d); WORKS="$WORKS $M"
    81	sed 's/^for m in defaults root metrics headless dash lane openwatch;/for m in defaults root metrics headless;/' "$ROOT/bin/harness" > "$M/dropped"
    82	mkdir -p "$M/lib"; cp $LIBS "$M/lib/"
    83	OUT="control: unmutated copy"
    84	check "control: unmutated copy passes all_listed" all_listed "$ROOT/bin/harness" "$M/lib"
    85	check "control: unmutated copy passes eager_ok" eager_ok "$ROOT/bin/harness"
    86	OUT="mutant: dash dropped from the list"
    87	check "mutation: dropped list entry is caught" not all_listed "$M/dropped" "$M/lib"
    88	cp "$ROOT/bin/harness" "$M/lazy"
    89	printf '%s\n' '. "$HARNESS_LIB/harness-metrics.sh"' >> "$M/lazy"
    90	OUT="mutant: lazy source after the loader"
    91	check "mutation: lazy source is caught" not eager_ok "$M/lazy"
    92	# marker moved to EOF (every source is then "above" it) and a lazy function defined above the marker
    93	grep -v '^# end loader$' "$ROOT/bin/harness" > "$M/eof"; echo '# end loader' >> "$M/eof"
    94	OUT="mutant: marker at EOF"
    95	check "mutation: marker at EOF is caught" not eager_ok "$M/eof"
    96	awk '/^# end loader$/ { print "lazy() { :; }" } { print }' "$ROOT/bin/harness" > "$M/fnbefore"
    97	OUT="mutant: function defined before the marker"
    98	check "mutation: function before marker is caught" not eager_ok "$M/fnbefore"
    99	
   100	# test lint: `check LABEL [ a ] && <anything>` / `|| <anything>` runs the second command outside check (its
   101	# failure is not counted), and the `-q` form of not_grep passes a pattern slot to the wrong grep. Both are forbidden outside
   102	# a `bash -c '...'` string; lines marked lint-skip (this file's own patterns and plants) are exempt.
   103	# lint_tests FILE... prints offending lines; fails if any.
   104	lint_tests() {
   105	  OUT=$(grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*check .*\] (&&|\|\|) |not_grep -q' "$@" | grep -v 'bash -c' | grep -v 'lint-skip' | head -5)  # lint-skip

    15	  OUT=$(env -u HARNESS_ROLE -u HERDR_ENV -u TMUX ${e[@]+"${e[@]}"} PATH="$BIN:$HERE/../bin:/usr/bin:/bin:$(dirname "$(command -v jq)")" /bin/bash "$HARNESS" "$@" 2>&1); RC=$?; }

1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# Fake `claude -p` for tests/headless.test.sh. Not a real client.
     3	# $FAKE_CLAUDE_MODE: success|noreport|error|maxturns|slow<N>|hang|hangterm|hangpre|nostart|junk
     4	# $FAKE_CLAUDE_DENY=1 emits a permission_denied event + result denial (default none).
     5	# $FAKE_CLAUDE_RESUME_MISSING=1: a --resume run fails like an unknown session (no init, rc 1).
     6	# $FAKE_PERM sets init permissionMode (default auto). hangpre sleeps before any output.
     7	#   success   init + tool_use + result success; writes the report via $FAKE_REPORT_CMD
     8	#   noreport  like success, no report      error  result is_error (rc 1)
     9	#   maxturns  error_max_turns (rc 1)       slow<N> sleeps N*0.1s, then success
    10	#   hang      sleeps until killed (TERM -> rc 143)   nostart  rc 127, no output
    11	#   junk      non-JSON and unknown event types mixed in, then success
    12	# argv (%q) and stdin go to $FAKE_LOG; $FAKE_DIR/claude.n counts runs (session sess-<n>).
    13	set -u
    14	: "${FAKE_LOG:?}"; : "${FAKE_DIR:?}"
    15	mode=${FAKE_CLAUDE_MODE:-success}
    16	{ printf 'claude: '; printf '%q ' "$@"; printf '\n'; } >> "$FAKE_LOG"
    17	input=$(cat)
    18	[ -z "${FAKE_ENV_DUMP:-}" ] || env > "$FAKE_ENV_DUMP"   # tests/headless-bg.test.sh: what a background run inherits
    19	printf 'claude stdin: %s\n' "$input" >> "$FAKE_LOG"
    20	[ "$mode" != nostart ] || exit 127
    21	echo $$ > "$FAKE_DIR/claude.pid"
    22	echo $$ >> "$FAKE_DIR/claude.pids"   # every run, so tests kill exactly their own
    23	n=$(( $(cat "$FAKE_DIR/claude.n" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) + 1 )); echo "$n" > "$FAKE_DIR/claude.n"
    24	sid=sess-$n
    25	resume=""; prev=""
    26	for a in "$@"; do [ "$prev" != --resume ] || resume=$a; prev=$a; done
    27	[ -z "$resume" ] || sid=$resume
    28	if [ -n "$resume" ] && [ "${FAKE_CLAUDE_RESUME_MISSING:-}" = 1 ]; then   # real claude 2.1.312: result-only stream, rc 1
    29	  echo "No conversation found with session ID: $resume" >&2
    30	  printf '%s\n' '{"type":"result","subtype":"error_during_execution","is_error":true,"errors":["No conversation found with session ID: '"$resume"'"],"session_id":"'"$sid"'","permission_denials":[]}'
    31	  exit 1
    32	fi
    33	[ "$mode" != hangterm ] || { trap '' TERM; while :; do sleep 0.1; done; }   # ignores TERM: only KILL stops it
    34	[ "$mode" != hangpre ] || { trap 'exit 143' TERM; while :; do sleep 0.1; done; }
    35	ev() { printf '%s\n' "$1"; }
    36	ev '{"type":"system","subtype":"hook_started","hook_event":"Stop","hook_name":"Stop"}'
    37	ev '{"type":"system","subtype":"init","model":"fake-model","permissionMode":"'"${FAKE_PERM:-auto}"'","cwd":"'"$PWD"'","session_id":"'"$sid"'"}'
    38	ev '{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"echo hi"}}],"usage":{"input_tokens":10,"cache_creation_input_tokens":20,"cache_read_input_tokens":30}},"session_id":"'"$sid"'"}'
    39	result() { # subtype is_error — FAKE_CLAUDE_DENY=1 adds one permission_denied event + a result denial
    40	  local den='[]'
    41	  if [ "${FAKE_CLAUDE_DENY:-}" = 1 ]; then
    42	    den='[{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"rm -rf /tmp/x\nsecond line"}}]'
    43	    ev '{"type":"system","subtype":"permission_denied","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"rm -rf /tmp/x\nsecond line"},"decision_reason":"safetyCheck","message":"denied by safety check","session_id":"'"$sid"'"}'
    44	  fi
    45	  ev '{"type":"result","subtype":"'"$1"'","is_error":'"$2"',"num_turns":3,"duration_ms":1500,"total_cost_usd":0.0123,"session_id":"'"$sid"'","permission_denials":'"$den"'}'
    46	}
    47	case "$mode" in
    48	  hang) trap 'exit 143' TERM; while :; do sleep 0.1; done ;;
    49	  slow*) sleep "$(awk -v n="${mode#slow}" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", n * 0.1 }')"
    50	         [ -z "${FAKE_REPORT_CMD:-}" ] || /bin/bash -c "$FAKE_REPORT_CMD"
    51	         result success false; exit 0 ;;
    52	  junk) ev 'this is not json'; ev '{"type":"future_event","x":1}'; ev '{"type":"rate_limit_event"}'; ev '{broken' ;;
    53	esac
    54	case "$mode" in
    55	  error) result error_during_execution true; exit 1 ;;
    56	  maxturns) result error_max_turns true; exit 1 ;;
    57	  noreport) result success false; exit 0 ;;
    58	  *) [ -z "${FAKE_REPORT_CMD:-}" ] || /bin/bash -c "$FAKE_REPORT_CMD"
    59	     result success false; exit 0 ;;
    60	esac

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# conductor-gate.sh — PreToolUse hook for the Fable conductor.
3	#
4	# Role:   hook input agent_type -> conductor: gate; any other agent: allow
5	#         (only when agent_id is absent; a subagent, agent_id set, uses the env rule)
6	#         (workers run as analyst/implementer/reviewer/solo). Keying on the
7	#         agent, not the env, closes the inherited-worker-env hole: a
8	#         conductor hosted by a daemon that exported HARNESS_ROLE=worker is still
9	#         gated. Without agent_type, HARNESS_ROLE=worker allows (older hosts).
10	#         Harness checkout: the gate acts only where .harness/asks/ exists (nearest
11	#                                 dir from the cwd up to the .git dir; decision 0010).
12	#                                 Elsewhere it allows everything, before jq or parsing,
13	#                                 so it never touches a repo that does not use the harness.
14	#         otherwise            -> conductor rules below
15	# Output: nothing (allow) or a PreToolUse deny JSON on stdout. Always exit 0.
16	set -u
17	
18	# lib/harness-root.sh holds the one harness_root. Hooks are not symlinked (install.sh writes
19	# the repo paths into settings.json), so the lib sits at a fixed place next to this file.
20	case ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} in */*) hd=${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*} ;; *) hd=. ;; esac   # run as `bash name` from its dir
21	. "$(CDPATH= cd -P "$hd/../../lib" 2>/dev/null && pwd)/harness-root.sh" 2>/dev/null || LIB_MISSING=1
22	# end loader
23	
24	INPUT=$(cat)
25	
26	if [ -n "${LIB_MISSING:-}" ]; then
27	  # no lookup possible: deny only the conductor (it exists only in harness checkouts), allow the rest
28	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
29	  [ "$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r 'if type == "object" then (.agent_type // empty) else empty end' 2>/dev/null)" = conductor ] || exit 0
30	  printf '%s\n' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"conductor-gate: lib/harness-root.sh missing; rerun ./install.sh"}}'
31	  exit 0
32	fi
33	
34	DIR=$PWD
35	if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
36	  c=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r 'if type == "object" then (.cwd // empty) else empty end' 2>/dev/null)
37	  if [ -n "$c" ] && [ -d "$c" ]; then DIR=$c; fi
38	fi
39	harness_root "$DIR" >/dev/null || exit 0
40	
41	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
42	  # fail closed; static JSON because jq is unavailable
43	  printf '%s\n' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Conductor gate requires jq. Install jq, or run a worker session."}}'
44	  exit 0
45	fi

47	TOOL=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_name // empty' 2>/dev/null)
48	if [ $? -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$TOOL" ]; then
49	  # fail closed (decision 0005): a gate that allows what it cannot read is no gate
50	  echo "conductor-gate: unparseable hook input, denying" >&2
51	  printf '%s\n' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Conductor gate could not parse the hook input, so the call is denied. Retry, or delegate with /analyze or /implement."}}'
52	  exit 0
53	fi
54	
55	# agent_id is set only for subagents (and forked skills) inside a session. Their
56	# hook input carries their OWN agent_type (e.g. "tiny"), not the session's, so
57	# agent_type alone would wave a conductor's subagent through: the agent_id check
58	# catches it and falls back to the env rule.
59	AGENT=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.agent_type // empty' 2>/dev/null)
60	AGENT_ID=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.agent_id // empty' 2>/dev/null)
61	if [ -n "$AGENT" ] && [ -z "$AGENT_ID" ]; then
62	  [ "$AGENT" = conductor ] || exit 0
63	elif [ "${HARNESS_ROLE:-conductor}" = worker ]; then
64	  exit 0
65	fi
66	
67	CWD=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null)
68	[ -n "$CWD" ] || CWD=$PWD
69	CWD=${CWD%/}
70	SESSION_ID=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.session_id // empty' 2>/dev/null)
71	
72	# Fixed strings: never interpolate per-call data (keeps the prompt cache stable).
73	MSG_WRITE="Conductor cannot edit source. Delegate with the /implement skill (implementer worker). Direct writes are allowed only under docs/**/*.md, .harness/, and the .harness/ of a registered work folder (git worktree)."
74	MSG_READ="Conductor does not read source. Delegate with the /analyze skill (analyst worker) and read its report. Direct reads are allowed only under .harness/, docs/, and *.md files."
75	MSG_WATCH="harness watch is for a human terminal; the conductor reads the report (harness report <worker>, or harness wait <worker> to block until the run ends)."
76	MSG_BASH="Conductor shell is limited to ONE command per call: harness (also harness -C <dir> ..., harness lane ...); gh pr create|view|list|checks|comment|edit|merge (no api, no merge -d); gh issue create|list|view|comment|close|edit|reopen; git status / log / diff --stat / branch (list); git show --stat|--name-only <rev> or git show <rev>:<path> (path under .harness/ or docs/, or *.md); ls (no -R) and stat on any path; cat, head, tail -n N under .harness/ and docs/, in a work folder's .harness/, and of this session's Bash task output files (/private/tmp/claude-*/<slug>/<session_id>/tasks/*.output). No ; & | redirects, backticks or \$(. Delegate command execution with the /implement skill (implementer worker)."

78	# --- Bash allow/deny lists ---------------------------------------------------
79	# Each piece below is one alternative; they are joined with | into one regex.
80	
81	# Commands the conductor may run (matched against a whole masked segment).
82	BASH_ALLOW='harness( .*)?'                                        # delegation CLI
83	BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'gh( .*)?'                               # GitHub CLI (see GH_ALLOW, gh_segment_ok)
84	BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git status( (-[sb]+|--short|--branch|--porcelain(=v[12])?|--untracked-files=(no|normal|all)))*' # read-only git; no -v (prints diffs) ...
85	BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git log( .*)?'
86	BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git diff --stat( .*)?'                  # ... summaries only
87	BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git branch( (-a|-r|-v|--show-current))*'  # list only
88	BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git show( .*)?'                         # git_show_ok narrows it: --stat/--name-only, or rev:path
89	BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'(cat|head|tail)( [^ ]+)+'               # cat_ls_segment_ok checks the files
90	BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'(ls|stat)( [^ ]+)*'                     # listing and metadata, any path, never recursive
91	BASH_ALLOW="^($BASH_ALLOW)\$"
92	
93	# gh "<group> <subcommand>" pairs the conductor may run. api, run, repo,
94	# auth, browse, issue delete|transfer|pin, pr diff|checkout|status are not here.
95	GH_ALLOW='pr (create|view|list|checks|comment|edit|merge)'
96	GH_ALLOW="$GH_ALLOW|"'issue (create|list|view|comment|close|edit|reopen)'
97	
98	# git long options that are denied anywhere in a git segment.
99	GIT_DENY_LONG='output'                                            # writes files
100	GIT_DENY_LONG="$GIT_DENY_LONG|delete|move|copy"                   # mutates branches
101	GIT_DENY_LONG="$GIT_DENY_LONG|patch|unified|cc|binary|remerge-diff|dd|diff-merges|raw|check" # prints diff content
102	
103	# Initials of git short-flag groups that are denied (e.g. -D, -Df, -U3):
104	#   o = --output (writes files)
105	#   d D m M c C = branch delete / move / copy (mutates branches)
106	#   p u U = patch / unified context (prints diff content)
107	#   G S = git log pickaxe (probes file contents)
108	GIT_DENY_SHORT='odDmMcCpuUGS'
109	
110	GIT_DENY="--($GIT_DENY_LONG)| -[$GIT_DENY_SHORT][A-Za-z0-9]* "
111	
112	deny() {
113	  jq -n --arg r "$1" \
114	    '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
115	  exit 0
116	}
117	
118	field() { printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r ".tool_input.$1 // empty" 2>/dev/null; }
119	
120	# rel PATH -> prints the path relative to CWD, or returns 1 when the path is
121	# empty, outside CWD, or contains a '..' segment.
122	rel() {
123	  local p=$1
124	  [ -n "$p" ] || return 1
125	  case "$p" in
126	    ..|../*|*/..|*/../*|'~'*) return 1 ;;
127	  esac
128	  case "$p" in
129	    "$CWD")   p="." ;;
130	    "$CWD"/*) p=${p#"$CWD"/} ;;
131	    /*)       return 1 ;;

137	# physrel PATH -> prints the symlink-resolved path relative to the resolved CWD
138	# ("." for CWD itself); returns 1 when it resolves outside CWD, loops, or
139	# exceeds 16 symlink hops. Needs only cd -P / pwd -P / readlink (bash 3.2, BSD).
140	# A path that does not exist yet resolves through its nearest existing ancestor.
141	physrel() {
142	  local p=$1 root full
143	  root=$(physical "$CWD") || return 1
144	  case "$p" in /*) ;; *) p=$CWD/$p ;; esac
145	  full=$(physical "$p") || return 1

147	    "$root") printf '.' ;;
148	    "$root"/*) printf '%s' "${full#"$root"/}" ;;
149	    *) return 1 ;;
150	  esac

152	
153	# physical ABS_PATH -> prints the fully resolved absolute path
154	physical() {
155	  local p=$1 hops=0 ex tail par t
156	  while :; do
157	    ex=$p; tail=""
158	    while [ ! -e "$ex" ] && [ ! -L "$ex" ]; do
159	      [ "$ex" != / ] || return 1
160	      tail="/${ex##*/}$tail"
161	      ex=${ex%/*}
162	      [ -n "$ex" ] || ex=/
163	    done
164	    if [ -L "$ex" ]; then
165	      hops=$((hops + 1))
166	      [ "$hops" -le 16 ] || return 1
167	      t=$(readlink "$ex") || return 1
168	      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
169	      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
170	      case "$t" in /*) p=$t$tail ;; *) p=$par/$t$tail ;; esac
171	      continue
172	    fi
173	    case "$tail" in */..|*/../*) return 1 ;; esac
174	    if [ -d "$ex" ]; then
175	      par=$(cd -P "$ex" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
176	      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '%s' "$tail"; else printf '%s' "$par$tail"; fi
177	    else
178	      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
179	      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
180	      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '/%s%s' "${ex##*/}" "$tail"; else printf '%s/%s%s' "$par" "${ex##*/}" "$tail"; fi
181	    fi
182	    return 0
183	  done

186	# readable_rel / writable_rel REL -> 0 when the repo-relative path is allowed

189	raw_stream_rel() {

192	  case "$l" in .harness/log/*.jsonl|.harness/log/*.jsonl.*) return 0 ;; esac

199	  esac

219	# lane_harness_path PATH -> 0 when PATH, symlinks resolved, is under .harness/ of
220	# a registered worktree of this repo (raw streams excluded). A relative PATH
221	# resolves against CWD; a '..' segment is denied.

227	    /*) ;;
228	    *) p=$CWD/$p ;;
229	  esac

233	    wr=$(physical "$wt") || continue

237	        rest=${full#"$wr"/}

240	    esac

247	# readable PATH -> 0 when the conductor may read it (lexically and after
248	# resolving symlinks)
249	readable() {
250	  local p
251	  p=$(rel "$1") || return 1
252	  readable_rel "$p" || return 1
253	  p=$(physrel "$1") || return 1
254	  readable_rel "$p"
255	}

258	readable_or_lane() { readable "$1" || lane_harness_path "$1"; }

260	# writable PATH -> 0 when the conductor may write it (lexically and after
261	# resolving symlinks), or it is under .harness/ of a registered work folder
262	writable() {
263	  local p
264	  if p=$(rel "$1") && writable_rel "$p" && p=$(physrel "$1") && writable_rel "$p"; then
265	    return 0
266	  fi

268	}
269	
270	# scan_command -> reads ONE command on stdin, scans it like the shell (single
271	# quotes, double quotes, backslash escapes) and prints "<masked><TAB><raw>".
272	# <masked> is the command with the contents of every '...' / "..." removed
273	# (quote chars kept); <raw> is the text as written. Exits 1 (= deny) on anything
274	# that would make it more than one simple command: an unquoted ; & | < > # `
275	# or newline, an unquoted $( $' $", ` or $( inside double quotes, an
276	# unterminated quote. Newlines inside quotes are kept as spaces.
277	# Input must not contain tabs (callers normalize them to spaces).
278	scan_command() {
279	  awk '
280	    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; m = ""; r = ""; nl = 0 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double
281	    {
282	      line = $0; n = length(line)
283	      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
284	        c = substr(line, i, 1); nx = substr(line, i + 1, 1)
285	        if (st == 0) {
286	          if (c == "\\") { c = c substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++; m = m c; r = r c }
287	          else if (c == ";" || c == "&" || c == "|" || c == "<" || c == ">" || c == "#" || c == "`") bad = 1
288	          else if (c == "$" && (nx == "(" || nx == "\047" || nx == "\"")) bad = 1
289	          else {
290	            m = m c; r = r c
291	            if (c == "\047") st = 1
292	            else if (c == "\"") st = 2
293	          }
294	        } else if (st == 1) {
295	          r = r c
296	          if (c == "\047") { m = m c; st = 0 }
297	        } else {
298	          r = r c
299	          if (c == "\\") { r = r substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++ }
300	          else if (c == "\"") { m = m c; st = 0 }
301	          else if (c == "`" || (c == "$" && nx == "(")) bad = 1
302	        }
303	      }
304	      if (st == 0) nl++; else r = r " "
305	    }
306	    END { if (st != 0 || bad || nl > 1) exit 1; print m "\t" r }
307	  '
308	}
309	
310	
311	# has_expansion TEXT -> 0 when TEXT contains a character that the shell would
312	# expand or glob ($ { } * ? [ ] ~ \)
313	has_expansion() {
314	  case "$1" in
315	    *[\$\{\}\*\?\[\]~\\]*) return 0 ;;
316	  esac
317	  return 1
318	}
319	
320	# git_segment_ok RAW -> 0 when a git segment uses no denied option and no
321	# rev:path (flag checks run on the raw text with quoting removed: "-D" == -D)
322	git_segment_ok() {
323	  local norm
324	  norm=$(printf ' %s ' "$1" | tr -d "\"'\\\\")
325	  case "$norm" in *:*) return 1 ;; esac
326	  printf '%s' "$norm" | grep -Eq -- "$GIT_DENY" && return 1
327	  return 0
328	}
329	
330	# plain_tok TOKEN -> 0 when TOKEN has no quote or backslash
331	plain_tok() {
332	  case "$1" in *[\"\'\\]*) return 1 ;; esac
333	  return 0
334	}
335	
336	# bodyfile_ok VALUE -> 0 when a gh --body-file / -F value is a path that stays
337	# (symlinks resolved) under .harness/ or docs/. "-" (stdin) is denied.
338	bodyfile_ok() {
339	  local v=$1 p
340	  [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != - ] || return 1
341	  plain_tok "$v" || return 1
342	  has_expansion "$v" && return 1
343	  p=$(rel "$v") || return 1
344	  p=$(physrel "$v") || return 1
345	  raw_stream_rel "$p" && return 1
346	  case "$p" in .harness/*|docs/*) return 0 ;; esac
347	  return 1
348	}
349	
350	# gh_segment_ok MASKED RAW -> 0 only for "gh pr|issue <sub>" with <sub> in GH_ALLOW
351	# (merge without -d). Global flags -R/--repo/--hostname (and --x=y) may precede
352	# the group. Everything up to and including the subcommand is read from the
353	# MASKED segment and must be plain unquoted tokens, so quoting cannot make this
354	# parser disagree with gh. --body-file/-F values must be plain paths under
355	# .harness/ or docs/. Flag checks on the rest of the segment use the raw text
356	# with quoting removed, so "--delete-branch" == --delete-branch.
357	gh_segment_ok() {
358	  local norm tok group sub nflag=0 mflag=0 want=0 v
359	  norm=$(printf '%s ' "$2" | tr -d "\"'\\\\" | tr -s ' ')
360	  set -f
361	  set -- $1
362	  set +f
363	  shift   # "gh"
364	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
365	    plain_tok "$1" || return 1
366	    case "$1" in
367	      -R|--repo|--hostname) [ $# -ge 2 ] || return 1; plain_tok "$2" || return 1; shift 2 ;;
368	      --repo=*|--hostname=*) shift ;;
369	      -*) return 1 ;;
370	      *) break ;;
371	    esac
372	  done
373	  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
374	  group=$1
375	  shift
376	  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
377	  sub=$1
378	  shift
379	  plain_tok "$sub" || return 1
380	  printf '%s' "$group $sub" | grep -Eq "^($GH_ALLOW)\$" || return 1
381	  # --body-file / -F values (also --body-file=x, -Fx, clusters like -dF): read
382	  # from the masked tail, must be plain paths under .harness/ or docs/
383	  for tok in "$@"; do
384	    if [ "$want" -eq 1 ]; then want=0; bodyfile_ok "$tok" || return 1; continue; fi
385	    case "$tok" in
386	      --body-file|--recover) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); want=1 ;;
387	      --body-file=*|--recover=*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); bodyfile_ok "${tok#*=}" || return 1 ;;
388	      --*) ;;
389	      -*F*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); v=${tok#*F}
390	            if [ -n "$v" ]; then bodyfile_ok "$v" || return 1; else want=1; fi ;;
391	    esac
392	  done
393	  [ "$want" -eq 0 ] || return 1
394	  # quote-stripped view: a flag that only appears once quotes are removed
395	  # ("--body-file") must not slip past the check above, and the per-command
396	  # flag denials apply to it
397	  set -f
398	  set -- $norm
399	  set +f
400	  for tok in "$@"; do
401	    case "$tok" in
402	      --body-file|--body-file=*|--recover|--recover=*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
403	      --delete-branch|--delete-branch=*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
404	      --*) ;;
405	      -*F*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
406	    esac
407	    case "$tok" in
408	      --*) ;;
409	      -*d*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
410	    esac
411	  done
412	  [ "$nflag" -le "$mflag" ] || return 1
413	  return 0
414	}
415	
416	# unquoted_text_ok RAW -> 0 when the segment's shell text is plain. Outside
417	# quotes only A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ / @ % + , : - = and spaces are allowed, and a word
418	# may not start with = (zsh =cmd) or ~. That rules out braces, globs, glob
419	# qualifiers, expansions, backslashes, redirects and history bangs in one go.
420	# Single-quoted text is literal. Double-quoted text may not contain $ ` \ or !.
421	unquoted_text_ok() {
422	  printf '%s\n' "$1" | LC_ALL=C awk '
423	    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; ws = 1 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double; ws: still at word start
424	    { n = length($0)
425	      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
426	        c = substr($0, i, 1)
427	        if (st == 1) { if (c == "\047") st = 0; else ws = 0 }
428	        else if (st == 2) {
429	          if (c == "\"") st = 0
430	          else {
431	            ws = 0
432	            if (c == "$" || c == "`" || c == "\\" || c == "!") bad = 1
433	          }
434	        } else if (c == " ") ws = 1
435	        else if (c == "\047") st = 1            # quotes alone do not end word start
436	        else if (c == "\"") st = 2
437	        else if (c == "\\") {                   # only \'"'"', \" and "\ " are literal
438	          nx = substr($0, i + 1, 1)
439	          if (nx == "\047" || nx == "\"" || nx == " ") { i++; ws = 0 } else bad = 1
440	        }
441	        else if (c ~ /[A-Za-z0-9._\/@%+,:-]/) ws = 0
442	        else if (c == "=" && !ws) ws = 0
443	        else bad = 1
444	      } }
445	    END { exit (bad || st != 0) ? 1 : 0 }'
446	}
447	
448	# commit_rev_ok REV -> 0 when REV is a plain rev (letters, digits . _ / @ -, then
449	# optional ~N / ^N suffixes) that resolves to a commit; a blob or tree SHA is
450	# denied because git show would print its content
451	commit_rev_ok() {
452	  case "$1" in
453	    ''|-*) return 1 ;;
454	  esac
455	  printf '%s' "$1" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9._/@-]+([~^][0-9]*)*$' || return 1
456	  git -C "$CWD" rev-parse -q --verify "$1^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1
457	}
458	
459	# git_show_ok MASKED -> 0 for "git show --stat|--name-only [REV...]" (no other
460	# option) or "git show REV:PATH" (one token; PATH under .harness/ or docs/, or
461	# *.md, no '..' segment, no raw stream). Tokens are plain: no quotes.
462	git_show_ok() {
463	  local tok rev path stat=0
464	  case "$1" in *[\"\']*) return 1 ;; esac
465	  set -f
466	  set -- $1
467	  set +f
468	  shift; shift   # git show
469	  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
470	  if [ $# -eq 1 ]; then
471	    case "$1" in
472	      *:*)
473	        rev=${1%%:*}; path=${1#*:}
474	        [ -n "$rev" ] && [ -n "$path" ] || return 1
475	        commit_rev_ok "$rev" || return 1
476	        case "$path" in *:*|/*|..|../*|*/..|*/../*) return 1 ;; esac
477	        raw_stream_rel "$path" && return 1
478	        case "$path" in .harness/*|docs/*|*.md) return 0 ;; esac
479	        return 1 ;;
480	    esac
481	  fi
482	  for tok in "$@"; do
483	    case "$tok" in
484	      --stat|--name-only) stat=1 ;;
485	      -*|*:*) return 1 ;;
486	      *) commit_rev_ok "$tok" || return 1 ;;
487	    esac
488	  done
489	  [ "$stat" -eq 1 ]
490	}
491	
492	# task_output_ok PATH -> 0 for a task output file of the calling session:
493	# /private/tmp/claude-*/<slug>/<session_id>/tasks/*.output (absolute, symlinks resolved)
494	task_output_ok() {
495	  local full rest a b c d e
496	  case "$SESSION_ID" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*) return 1 ;; esac
497	  case "$1" in /*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
498	  full=$(physical "$1") || return 1
499	  case "$full" in /private/tmp/claude-*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
500	  rest=${full#/private/tmp/}
501	  IFS=/ read -r a b c d e <<RESTEOF
502	$rest
503	RESTEOF
504	  case "$a" in claude-*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
505	  [ -n "$b" ] && [ "$c" = "$SESSION_ID" ] && [ "$d" = tasks ] || return 1
506	  case "$e" in ''|*/*|*[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) return 1 ;; esac
507	  case "$e" in *.output) return 0 ;; esac
508	  return 1
509	}
510	
511	# cat_ls_segment_ok MASKED -> 0 when a cat / ls segment needs no quoting,
512	# expansion or parent-directory access
513	cat_ls_segment_ok() {
514	  local tok p cmd=${1%% *}
515	  case "$1" in *[\"\']*|*..*) return 1 ;; esac
516	  has_expansion "$1" && return 1
517	  set -f
518	  set -- $1
519	  set +f
520	  case "$1" in
521	    ls|stat)             # any path: listing and metadata only, never recursive
522	      shift
523	      for tok in "$@"; do
524	        case "$tok" in
525	          --r*) return 1 ;;            # --recursive (and abbreviations)
526	          --*) ;;
527	          -*R*) return 1 ;;            # -R, -laR, ...
528	        esac
529	      done ;;
530	    cat|head|tail)
531	      shift
532	      if [ "${1:-}" = -n ] && [ "$cmd" != cat ]; then   # head/tail: optional "-n N" only (no -f)
533	        case "${2:-}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
534	        shift 2
535	      fi
536	      [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
537	      for tok in "$@"; do
538	        case "$tok" in -*) return 1 ;; esac
539	        # symlink-resolved: .harness/ or docs/ here, a task output file, or a work folder's .harness/
540	        if p=$(physrel "$tok") && ! raw_stream_rel "$p"; then
541	          case "$p" in .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*) continue ;; esac
542	        fi
543	        task_output_ok "$tok" && continue
544	        lane_harness_path "$tok" && continue
545	        return 1
546	      done ;;
547	  esac
548	  return 0
549	}
550	
551	# bash_ok COMMAND -> 0 when COMMAND is one simple command on the allowlist
552	bash_ok() {
553	  local cmd=$1 out seg raw tab
554	  tab=$(printf '\t')
555	  [ -n "$cmd" ] || return 1
556	  cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | tr '\t' ' ')
557	  out=$(printf '%s\n' "$cmd" | scan_command) || return 1
558	  seg=${out%%"$tab"*}
559	  raw=${out#*"$tab"}
560	  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
561	  raw=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
562	  [ -n "$seg" ] || return 1
563	  # plain shell text only (character allowlist); in a git show segment ~N / ^N rev
564	  # suffixes are exempt here (commit_rev_ok validates them strictly)
565	  case "$seg" in
566	    git\ show|git\ show\ *) unquoted_text_ok "$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed -E 's/([A-Za-z0-9._@-])([~^][0-9]*)+/\1/g')" || return 1 ;;
567	    *) unquoted_text_ok "$raw" || return 1 ;;
568	  esac
569	  # reject '..' path components (but not git ranges like main...HEAD)
570	  printf ' %s ' "$seg" | grep -Eq '[ /=]\.\.([ /]|$)' && return 1
571	  case "$seg" in
572	    git\ show|git\ show\ *) git_show_ok "$seg" || return 1 ;;
573	    git\ *)          git_segment_ok "$raw" || return 1
574	                     ;;
575	    gh|gh\ *)        gh_segment_ok "$seg" "$raw" || return 1 ;;
576	    cat\ *|head\ *|tail\ *|ls|ls\ *|stat\ *) cat_ls_segment_ok "$seg" || return 1 ;;
577	  esac
578	  printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq "$BASH_ALLOW"
579	}
580	
581	case "$TOOL" in
582	  Edit|Write)
583	    writable "$(field file_path)" || deny "$MSG_WRITE" ;;
584	  Read)
585	    readable_or_lane "$(field file_path)" || deny "$MSG_READ" ;;
586	  Grep)
587	    readable "$(field path)" || deny "$MSG_READ"
588	    # a directory search would read the raw streams under .harness/log
589	    GRP=$(physrel "$(field path)") || deny "$MSG_READ"
590	    case "$GRP" in .harness|.harness/log) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac ;;
591	  Glob)
592	    PATTERN=$(field pattern)
593	    case "$PATTERN" in *..*|/*|'~'*) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac
594	    GPATH=$(field path)
595	    if [ -z "$GPATH" ]; then
596	      # no path: the pattern itself must stay under .harness/ or docs/
597	      case "$PATTERN" in docs/*|.harness/*) ;; *) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac
598	      GBASE=$CWD
599	    else
600	      readable "$GPATH" || deny "$MSG_READ"
601	      GBASE=$GPATH
602	      case "$GBASE" in /*) ;; *) GBASE=$CWD/$GBASE ;; esac
603	    fi
604	    # resolve the pattern's static directory prefix (up to the first glob char)
605	    GPRE=${PATTERN%%[\*\?\[\{]*}
606	    if [ "$GPRE" = "$PATTERN" ]; then GDIR=$PATTERN
607	    else case "$GPRE" in */*) GDIR=${GPRE%/*} ;; *) GDIR="" ;; esac
608	    fi
609	    GP=$(physrel "$GBASE${GDIR:+/$GDIR}") || deny "$MSG_READ"
610	    case "$GP" in .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*) ;; *) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac ;;
611	  Bash)
612	    BCMD=$(field command)
613	    printf '%s' "$BCMD" | grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*harness[[:space:]]+(-C[[:space:]]+("[^"]*"|'"'"'[^'"'"']*'"'"'|[^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+)?["'"'"']?watch["'"'"']?([[:space:]]|$)' && deny "$MSG_WATCH"
614	    bash_ok "$BCMD" || deny "$MSG_BASH" ;;
615	esac
616	
617	exit 0
618
